newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Rebels free Indonesian crew of Sri Lanka ship.
newsitem.headline: Rebels free Indonesian crew of Sri Lanka ship.

text.p: Tamil rebels on Friday released two Indonesian crew members of a Sri Lankan civilian refugee ship three days after they were seized off the island's northwest coast, military officials said.
The rebels had forced their way on to the MV Missen and taken away its captain Nang Hadi, chief engineer Imam Wahudin and nine crew, the officials said. The rebels then torched the ship.

The two Indonesians were freed following intervention by International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), which said in a statement it had secured their release by acting as a neutral intermediary. It did not give further details.

Aid workers in Vavuniya, a government-held town some 220 km (135 miles) north of the capital Colombo, said the crew were released by the Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels in Malavi, northwest of Vavuniya.
They said the two were being brought to Colombo and would be handed over to the Indonesian Embassy.
The fate of the remaining seven crew, all Sri Lankans, was not immediately known, officials and the ICRC said.
"The ICRC remains deeply concerned regarding the fate of the seven remaining members of the crew and is taking all necessary steps to be able to see them as soon as possible," the ICRC statment said.
The LTTE were not immediately available for comment, but a spokesman in London on Tuesday denied that the rebels had destroyed the ship and taken away the crew.

The government has said the rebels torched the vessel in an attempt to discourage refugees in the Wanni region to return to Jaffna, where the government is rehabilitating several hundred thousand people who fled when the military captured the former rebel stronghold last year.

The LTTE are fighting for a separate homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more tha 50,000 people have been killed in the war. The LTTE say the toll is higher.
